title: Open finite-image kernel and derived quotient inflation for norm-topological coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F=E,\Omega$, set $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], on the small coherent profinite site [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite group $P$ let $\mathcal A_P(C_F)$ be the category of internal $C_F$-modules with linear condensed $P$-action and normalized invariant equalizers [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories and K-injective total right derived invariants $R\Gamma_P$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and the normalized inflation arrows [def-sfb-condensed-derived-inflation-arrows].

Let $B,L$ be profinite groups such that every finite continuous quotient of $B$ has order prime to $\ell$. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space with continuous $E$-linear $B\times L$-action and finite $B$-image $Q\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_E(V)$. Put $K=\ker(B\to Q)$ and $V_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E V)$, with finite-dimensional product norm topology [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation]. Then $K$ is open and normal, $B/K\simeq Q$ as finite topological groups, and every finite continuous quotient of $K$ has order prime to $\ell$. The $K$-action on $V_F$ is trivial and $V_F\simeq C_F^d$ as $K$-modules, where $d=\dim_E V$.

For both $F$, the canonical augmentation and the canonical quotient inflation are isomorphisms in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$:
$$V_F[0]\longrightarrow R\Gamma_K(V_F[0]),\qquad t_F:R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(V_F[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{B\times L}(V_F[0]).$$
In the first arrow $V_F$ is restricted to $K$; in the source of the second it carries the residual $Q\times L$-action. The second arrow is induced by $B\times L\to Q\times L$ and the identity on the underlying module. It is normalized by the invariant inclusion. Rank zero and trivial $K$ or $Q$ are allowed. The statement uses the norm topology on $\Omega$ without completing it.

proof.text:
For each nonidentity $q\in Q$ choose $v_q\in V$ with $qv_q
e v_q$ and an open set $W_q\subseteq V$ containing $v_q$ but not $qv_q$; this is possible since $V$ is Hausdorff. Continuity of the action makes $O_q=\{b\in B:bv_q\in W_q\}$ open. Then $K= igcap_{q
e1}O_q$: elements of $K$ lie in every $O_q$, whereas an element with image $q
e1$ fails the condition indexed by that $q$. This is a finite intersection, so $K$ is open. It is normal as a homomorphism kernel. Each of its other cosets is open, hence $K$ is also closed and is profinite with the inherited topology. The topology on $Q$ is discrete: distinct linear operators are separated by evaluation on a vector in the Hausdorff norm topology, and a finite Hausdorff subspace is discrete (remove its other finitely many closed points). The quotient homomorphism $B	o Q$ is continuous, since all its fibres are open cosets of $K$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the finite-image kernel input: finite evaluation tests isolate the open kernel

proof.text: The assignment $bK\mapsto\rho(b)$ is a well-defined bijective group homomorphism $B/K\to Q$: equality of images is exactly membership of $b^{-1}b'$ in $K$. Every coset of $K$ is open, so $B/K$ is discrete; it is finite because it is bijective to $Q$. The bijection and its inverse are therefore continuous. Now let $K\twoheadrightarrow H$ be any finite continuous quotient and put $J$ equal to its open normal kernel. Since $K$ is open in $B$, $J$ is open in $B$. Its open cosets cover the compact group $B$, so $[B:J]$ is finite. The conjugates of $J$ are indexed by the finite coset set $B/J$ (two representatives of the same left coset give the same conjugate); hence their intersection $U=\bigcap_{b\in B}bJb^{-1}$ is open normal in $B$ and lies in $J\subseteq K$. By hypothesis $|B/U|$ is prime to $\ell$. The subgroup $K/U$ has order dividing $|B/U|$, since its cosets partition $B/U$ into equal-sized sets. Likewise $|K/J|$ divides $|K/U|$ by counting cosets of $J/U$. As $H\simeq K/J$, its order is prime to $\ell$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the finite-image kernel input: finite quotient identification and the normal-core argument

proof.text: Write $A=C_F$ and $N=V_F$. Every element of $K$ acts identically on $V$, hence on $F\otimes_E V$. For any profinite $S$ and any $g:S\to K$, the action on sections is $(g\cdot f)(s)=\rho_F(g(s))f(s)=f(s)$ by [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]; the same holds after every base change. Thus the condensed $K$-action is trivial. The chosen basis identifies the actual tensor-product vector space $F\otimes_E V$ with $F^d$, with the finite-dimensional product norm topology stipulated in the statement. Taking coordinates gives mutually inverse $A(S)$-linear maps $C(S,F\otimes_E V)\leftrightarrow C(S,F)^d$, compatible with every restriction and with trivial $K$-actions. These define $N\simeq A^d$ as $K$-modules. The argument is valid for $F=\Omega$ without completeness.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the finite-image kernel input: basis coordinates on the actual all-continuous realization

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-prime-to-ell-condensed-acyclicity] to the profinite group $K$ using step 2. It gives an invertible canonical augmentation $A[0]\to R\Gamma_K(A[0])$ for each $F$. This implies the finite-rank augmentation, with its actual normalization, as follows. Choose a K-injective resolution $A[0]\to I$ as in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. A finite direct sum $I^{\oplus d}$ is K-injective: a chain map from an acyclic complex into it is a tuple of $d$ maps into $I$, and a tuple of their null homotopies is a null homotopy. The map $A^d[0]\to I^{\oplus d}$ is a quasi-isomorphism because kernels, images and cohomology of a finite direct sum are computed coordinatewise. The invariant equalizer preserves this sum, also coordinatewise. Hence the augmentation for $A^d$ is the sum of the $d$ scalar augmentations. Naturality with the coordinate inclusions and projections identifies it with this sum; the derived functor is additive by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Its inverse is the sum of the scalar inverses. Transport along step 3 proves that the specified $N[0]\to R\Gamma_K(N[0])$ is invertible. For $d=0$, the resolution and both sides are zero and their unique map is an isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the finite-image kernel input: scalar augmentation extended to finite rank with its resolution normalization

proof.text: Identify $Q$ with $B/K$ by step 2. Use [lem-sfb-derived-invariants-normal-subgroup-comparison] with $G=B$, this open normal $K$, the given $L$, and $A=C_F$. Put $T(M)=M^K$ retaining the $Q\times L$-action, and let $U$ forget that residual action. By step 3 every section of $N$ is fixed after every profinite base change, so the invariant inclusion identifies $T(N)$ with $N$. Its residual $Q\times L$-action is the quotient action from the exact normalized adjunction in the cited comparison; no splitting of $B\to Q$ is chosen. The comparison gives $\beta:D(U)RT(N[0])\simeq R\Gamma_K(N[0])$ and a unit $\eta_N:T(N)[0]\to RT(N[0])$ whose underlying map is precisely the augmentation proved invertible in step 4. Choose a K-injective resolution $i:N[0]\to I$. By [lem-sfb-normal-inflation-resolution-naturality], $\eta_N$ is represented by $T(i)$, and under $\beta$ its underlying map is the usual invariant-resolution augmentation. These are statements about the specified maps, not merely isomorphism classes of their source and target.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the finite-image kernel input: normalized residual kernel unit

proof.text: Write $\mathsf q$ for localization of complexes, to distinguish it from the finite group $Q$. The underlying map $\mathsf q(U(T(i)))$ is invertible by steps 4 and 5. Each cohomology functor factors through localization by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so every $H^r(U(T(i)))$ is an isomorphism. Forgetting actions creates kernels and cokernels and detects exactness by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]; it therefore computes cohomology on the underlying modules. It also reflects isomorphisms: the inverse of an equivariant module isomorphism is equivariant, by multiplying the equivariance identity by the inverse on both sides. It follows that every $H^r(T(i))$ is an isomorphism. Thus $T(i)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and its localization $\eta_N$ is invertible, by the definition of quasi-isomorphism and localization in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the finite-image kernel input: detection of the kernel unit on cohomology after forgetting actions

proof.text: The same normal-subgroup comparison supplies an isomorphism $c_N:R\Gamma_{B\times L}(N[0])\simeq R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(RT(N[0]))$ and the exact normalization equation $c_N\operatorname{inf}_N=R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(\eta_N)$ [lem-sfb-derived-invariants-normal-subgroup-comparison]. The right side is invertible by step 6, so $\operatorname{inf}_N=c_N^{-1}R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(\eta_N)$ is invertible. Its defining coefficient morphism is $\operatorname{Inf}T(N)\hookrightarrow N$, which under $T(N)=N$ is the identity. Consequently it is exactly the quotient inflation $t_F$ of [def-sfb-condensed-derived-inflation-arrows]. Its degree-zero normalization is the invariant inclusion, as specified by the comparison. Applying this argument separately to $F=E,\Omega$ proves both claims. If $K=1$ the kernel comparison and unit are identities; if $Q=1$ the quotient is the trivial group and the same equation applies. Rank zero was covered in step 4.
